s01.text: Quantization can be done after training, by rounding the weights of a finished model.

s02.text: Or it can be done during training, by rounding the weights on every step.

s03.text: The second one is slower to set up and much better in the result.

s04.text: Here is why. A trained model has never seen a rounded weight.

s05.text: The weights sit in a narrow band where the network is sensitive. Round them, and you move them.

s06.text: Move them far enough and the next layer gets a different input than it was trained for.

s07.text: One layer's rounding error becomes the next layer's noise, and it compounds.

s08.text: Training with quantization in the loop teaches the model to work with rounded weights.

s09.text: It learns to put its important information in the places where rounding does the least damage.

s10.text: So the gap between the two is not a small margin. It is the difference between working and not.

s11.text: Which is also why the honest version of a quantization claim has to say which one was used.

s12.text: A number from a post-training model and a number from a quantization-aware one are not the same number.

s13.text: Ask how the model was trained before you believe the size.
